question: How does calloc() differ from malloc() in terms of the memory it returns?
options: calloc() zero-initializes the allocated memory, while malloc() leaves it uninitialized
calloc() is only usable for char arrays
They behave identically in every way
explanation: calloc(count, size) both allocates memory and initializes every byte to zero, whereas malloc(size) allocates memory whose initial contents are indeterminate.
